title: Credit and Collections Policy: Disconnect Notices and Disconnection for Nonpayment of Electric Service by Rate Schedule
content:
**1. Notice.** A disconnect notice is issued on an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account when a bill's past-due amount, plus any earlier unpaid past-due amounts, is at least the schedule's disconnect notice threshold and is still unpaid the schedule's notice days after the due date, in calendar days. The notice records its issue date and the past-due amount it demands. Notices are never issued for program charges of a PrePay Power-enrolled account or for amounts under a budget plan deferral.

**2. Notice period.** Disconnection may be performed only when the schedule's notice period, in calendar days, has passed since the disconnect notice was issued. The days are counted from the day after the notice date, the earliest disconnection day being the last day of the count. The record that starts the clock is the notice date on the service account.

**3. Medical protection.** Disconnection is never performed while the service account's medical certificate protection date is on or after the current date.

**4. Pledges and arrangements.** Disconnection is never performed while energy assistance pledges recorded within the schedule's pledge hold days cover the past-due amount on the notice, nor while an active payment arrangement on the same service account is in good standing. The pledges counted are those recorded in the hold period ending on the current date, less the agency payments from the same agency posted on or after each pledge's date. The arrangement is read from the Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements) record of the same service account.

**5. Days and hours.** Disconnection is performed only on weekdays that are not cooperative holidays, between the start and end of business hours, never on the day before a cooperative holiday, and on a Friday only where the schedule permits Friday disconnection.

**6. Field collection.** When the field representative sent to disconnect collects the full past-due amount at the meter instead, the meter stays on, the notice is cleared and the schedule's field collection fee is charged. A partial collection at the meter does not have that effect.

### Notice period — boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Schedule and notice date | Notice period | Earliest disconnection day | The day before it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule R, notice dated May 1 | 10 calendar days | May 11 — permitted, subject to clauses 3 to 5 | May 10 — not permitted |
| Schedule GS-1, notice dated May 1 | 7 calendar days | May 8 — permitted, subject to clauses 3 to 5 | May 7 — not permitted |

### Points of judgement

- The notice period, the medical protection, the pledge hold, the arrangement and the day-and-hour limits are separate conditions on performing a disconnection; a disconnection is performed only on a day on which none of them bars it.
- Each schedule's notice threshold, notice period, Friday rule and medical certificate availability are its own figures in the collection and member protection tables.
